situation:
You are the financial manager for HARROW BEND FURNITURE COMPANY, a manufacturer of solid-wood dining and bedroom furniture. The company is preparing to retool its main plant, and the vice president of finance (judge) has asked you to recommend how HARROW BEND FURNITURE COMPANY should raise the six million dollars the project requires.

HARROW BEND FURNITURE COMPANY has built furniture in the same town for forty years and sells through roughly three hundred independent dealers. A new entrant, FLATPINE HOME, has taken share for three straight years by shipping ready-to-assemble furniture directly to customers. Retooling would cut the company's production time nearly in half and let it quote delivery dates that match FLATPINE HOME's.

One route is a six-year bank loan. It leaves ownership of the company where it is, but the lender's terms require the company to hold more cash on hand, and the only way to reach that balance is to stretch payments to TIMBERWAY HARDWOODS from thirty days to ninety. TIMBERWAY HARDWOODS has supplied kiln-dried lumber for thirty years and says longer terms would cost the company its first claim on the seasonal supply.

The other route is selling a minority stake to CEDAR ROW CAPITAL. That cash arrives without debt and without stretched payments, but the investors would take two board seats and have already argued that the company should close its independent dealer channel and sell online instead. The vice president of finance (judge) wants you to compare the two routes, explain what each does to the company's financial reporting and its relationships, and recommend one.

You will present your analysis and your recommendation to the vice president of finance (judge) in the vice president's office. The vice president of finance (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After your presentation and your answers to the questions that follow, the vice president of finance (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of finance at HARROW BEND FURNITURE COMPANY, the solid-wood furniture manufacturer described above. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the financial manager to compare the six-year bank loan against the sale of a minority stake to CEDAR ROW CAPITAL, to show what each one does to the company's reporting, its supply of kiln-dried lumber and its dealer channel, and to recommend one of them.

After the presentation you will ask these two questions:
judgeQuestions: Two years from now, what would this decision have changed about the company?
If FLATPINE HOME keeps taking share after we retool, where does that leave us?
